name: Tisagenlecleucel
drug_class: CD19-directed autologous CAR T-cell therapy (4-1BB costimulation)
route_note: Single IV infusion of the patient's own genetically modified T cells after lymphodepleting chemotherapy
originator: University of Pennsylvania (Carl June, Bruce Levine, David Porter) with Novartis

discovery.by: Carl June and colleagues (University of Pennsylvania)
discovery.note: Lentiviral CAR combining an anti-CD19 scFv, a 4-1BB costimulatory domain and CD3ζ signalling.

tagline: First CAR T-cell therapy approved, for childhood leukaemia and B-cell lymphomas
summary: Tisagenlecleucel is a personalised gene-modified cell therapy in which a patient's T cells are engineered to express a chimeric antigen receptor against CD19. In 2017 it became the first CAR T-cell therapy and the first gene therapy approved in the US, for relapsed or refractory B-cell ALL in young patients.
mechanism: The patient's T cells are collected by leukapheresis and transduced with a lentiviral vector encoding a CAR: an anti-CD19 single-chain antibody fragment linked to 4-1BB and CD3ζ signalling domains.

After infusion, the CAR T cells recognise CD19 on malignant and normal B cells independently of MHC, become activated, proliferate and kill target cells. The 4-1BB domain supports long persistence, sometimes for years, accompanied by prolonged B-cell aplasia.
uses: Relapsed or refractory B-cell precursor ALL in patients up to 25 years
Relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma after two or more lines
Relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma after two or more lines

history.title: First patients
history.detail: Penn reports dramatic remissions in CLL with CTL019.

history.title: Emily Whitehead
history.detail: Emily Whitehead becomes the first child treated with CTL019 for ALL and remains in long-term remission.

history.title: Novartis alliance
history.detail: Novartis and Penn form an alliance to develop the therapy.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in August for paediatric and young adult B-ALL (ELIANA), the first CAR T-cell therapy approved.

history.title: Lymphoma and EU approval
history.detail: Approved for large B-cell lymphoma (JULIET); EU approval follows in August.

history.title: Follicular lymphoma
history.detail: Accelerated approval for relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma (ELARA).

history.title: T-cell malignancy warning
history.detail: FDA adds a boxed warning on secondary T-cell malignancies to all BCMA- and CD19-directed CAR T therapies.

history.title: REMS removed
history.detail: FDA eliminates the REMS requirements for approved autologous CAR T-cell therapies.

pk.half_life: CAR transgene persists for months to years (cellular kinetics, not classical half-life)
pk.metabolism: Cells expand in vivo after infusion and then contract

safety.boxed_warning: Cytokine release syndrome, neurological toxicities and T-cell malignancies; available only at certified treatment centres.

facts: Tisagenlecleucel was the first gene therapy of any kind approved by the FDA.
Tocilizumab was approved in 2017 specifically for CAR T-cell-induced cytokine release syndrome.
